summary: Suggests a method that lets existing IP addressing, including the IP protocol field, be used for the ISO Connectionless Network Protocol (CLNP). It is a draft answer to one problem of carrying "ISO-grams" in the DOD Internet, and asks for discussion. It was replaced by RFC 1069.

eli5.summary: Two groups use different address labels. This memo shows how to reuse the labels from one group on the other's packets so both can share the same network.

questions: how to use ip addresses with clnp
what is the icd for the dod internet
subtitle: A June 1986 working draft that shows how to build ISO CLNP addresses out of existing Internet IP addresses.

tldr.problem: The ISO Connectionless Network Protocol (CLNP) puts the identification of the user protocol inside the address, but the DOD Internet already had IP addresses and an IP protocol field.
tldr.mechanism: The memo defines an ISO address that embeds the four-byte IP address and the one-byte IP user protocol field, under an ISO-6523-ICD address format with ICD 0006 for the DOD Internet. A separate X.121-based format covers systems reached only through public data networks.
tldr.outcome: It was a working draft that asked for discussion, and it was obsoleted by RFC 1069.

today: RFC 986 was a working draft, and it was obsoleted by RFC 1069, which is where the guidance continued. Its status is listed as Unknown.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 986 suggests a method for using the existing IP addressing, including the IP protocol field, with the ISO Connectionless Network Protocol (CLNP). It calls this a draft solution to one of the problems of carrying "ISO-grams" in the DOD Internet, says related issues will be discussed in later RFCs, and asks for discussion and suggestions.

The memo reproduces the CLNP header only for completeness. The address part of that header, the destination and source addresses, is what the memo is about. It presents a specific way to address in the DOD Internetwork environment that stays consistent with the international standardized NSAP addresses.
sections.eli5: The memo is about the address label on a packet, not the rest of the packet. It explains how to write an Internet address in the label format the ISO world expects.

sections.title: Addresses for Use in the Internet
sections.content:
An NSAP address in the Internet starts with a one-octet Authority and Format Identifier (AFI) with the value 47, written in binary coded decimal. That value specifies an ISO-6523-ICD assignment and says the rest of the address is based on binary. The ICD format was chosen to emphasize that this is an administrative assignment. A Data Country Code would be possible but could be misleading, given the wide geographic spread of the Internet.

The next two octets are the Initial Domain Identifier, which holds the International Code Designator assigned to the DOD Internet. It must contain 0006. The rest is the Domain Specific Part, assigned by the Internet administration as an addressing domain. It has a one-byte version number, which must contain 01 and allows for future extensions, then the four-byte IP address, then the one-byte IP user protocol field.
sections.eli5: The new address is built like a nesting doll: first a code saying which kind of address it is, then a code for the Internet as a whole, then a version number, then the ordinary Internet address and a note about which program should get the packet.

sections.title: Why the User Protocol Is in the Address
sections.content:
The IP address used inside the ISO address is the same four-octet IP address in use at the time, and the user protocol field is the same as the user protocol field in the current IP header. The memo says it is necessary to include it because the ISO protocol treats identification of the user protocol as an addressing issue. It therefore does not allow the user protocol to be specified in the protocol header independently of the address.

Current IP addresses and user protocol numbers are to be found in the Assigned Numbers document, RFC 960.
sections.eli5: In the ISO system, the note saying which program should get the packet has to be written on the address label itself, so the memo copies it there.

sections.title: Devices Attached to Public Data Networks
sections.content:
Otherwise isolated end systems, and simple LANs that are attached to the Internet only through public data networks (PDNs), use a separate address format based on their X.121 address. Here the AFI specifies an ISO-X.121 address format with a binary Domain Specific Part. The AFI is a single octet that must take the value 37 (hexadecimal). The IDI contains the X.121 address encoded in binary (using BCD), padded at the end if necessary with all ones to make up 7 full octets. The DSP then holds a single octet naming the user protocol.

Simple LANs attached to PDNs use the same address with a variable-length local address added for the LAN. Whether an address is the end-system form or the LAN form is determined by looking at its length.
sections.eli5: Computers that only reach the Internet through a phone-company network use their phone-style number instead. A small local network adds its own extra room number at the end.
